question.text: The primary advantage of a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) in mutual funds is:

answer.text: Guaranteed returns over the investment period
Tax exemption on all SIP investments
Rupee cost averaging — buying more units when prices are low and fewer when high
Zero exit load on all SIP redemptions

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM-Series-X-A (p.218) describes rupee cost averaging as the primary advantage of SIPs: investing the same amount at regular intervals buys more units when NAV is low and fewer units when NAV is high, averaging the cost of acquisition over time. The Trap: SIPs do not provide guaranteed returns or blanket tax exemption — those are common misconceptions; the source-backed benefit is the averaging mechanism itself. Note: Wider claims (for example, when lump-sum may outperform SIP, or specific tax treatments) are not in the checked SIP pages and should be cited from a separate source before being asserted.
